structured.approach: Attempt 3 fixes the repeated G2 refusals. The cause was a repository-name mismatch, not a missing read. I had cited the local checkout folder names (file:ap_pipeline/…, file:ap_forecast/…, file:ap_aging/…, file:ap_portal/…). The read tracker records these files under their GitHub repository names: ap-pipeline-sample, ap-forecast-sample, ap-aging-sample and ap-portal-sample. I found this in this item's earlier REQ-07 step record (steps/FEAT-ZD-48600/REQ-07/judge_brief_attempt3.md, which lists the files read under those names). I re-read every cited code file again in this attempt and rewrote feat.trd in full. Every code citation now uses the GitHub repository name, and the header states the folder-to-repository mapping. The content is otherwise the same as the verified draft. It follows the org.templates TRD sections (components affected, interfaces/contracts, data, security and tenancy, testing approach, risks). It builds on cited code findings F-1 to F-15, which include two existing-code conflicts for the Architect. It ends with assumptions, questions TQ-1 to TQ-11, PRD traceability and a decision-log check. I also called context_list to confirm the step's contracted inputs. No connector was needed.

claims.text: The TRD follows the TRD template: components affected, interfaces/contracts, data, security and tenancy, testing approach, risks.

Architecture rule carried into the TRD: keep every existing signature and add new functions. ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging are Python 3.9; ap_portal is Node.js 22 CommonJS. JSON between services carries amounts as strings with two decimals and dates as ISO strings.

transform.to_model returns (records, rejected). Records are plain dicts with keys id, vendor, due_date, amount (Decimal, not quantised) and paid. A rejected row's reason is the exception type name, so the required reason 'paid_date' needs its own code path.
parse_feed returns each CSV row as a dict via csv.DictReader, so a feed without a paid_date column gives rows with no paid_date key.

pipeline.run(csv_text) returns a tuple of records and the quality report. quality_report collects reject reasons from the rejected rows, so 'paid_date' appears in reject_reasons without any change to dq.py.

predict_delay_days returns a rounded mean, returns 0 for an empty history, and counts negative delays as 0. So vendor_risk([]) returns 'low', and the negative delay_days kept by AC-6 do not lower the prediction below 0.
vendor_risk returns 'high' when predict_delay_days(history) > 30, 'medium' when it is > 10, otherwise 'low', and calls no LLM.

build_explanation_request(vendor, predicted_days, config=None) reads its provider and model from models.json (acme-llm, acme-text-2). The TRD adds risk=None as the last parameter, so that the prompt without risk is unchanged and with risk ends with ' Risk level: <risk>.'.

Conflict in existing code: bucket_for returns '1-30' only when days < 30, so exactly 30 days goes to '31-60'. The TRD forbids overdue_with_risk from using bucket_for and raises a fix as a separate question.
days_past_due counts calendar days after the due date. overdue_with_risk reuses it and lists unpaid invoices only when days > 30.
Conflict in existing code: ap_portal's exported formatAmount uses Number(value || 0).toFixed(2), which goes through a binary float against D-2026-044. renderOverdueRisk must not use it.
Each repository's CI requires compile, passing tests, coverage of at least 90% and static checks, including lines no longer than 140 characters.
ap_portal tests use node:test and load the package with require('ap_portal'). The existing formatAmount and renderAgingSummary tests must keep passing.
The proposed CT-1 JSON row carries id, vendor, days, amount as a two-decimal string, and risk. Example from the prototype: SYN-INV-004, Synthetic Vendor A, 75, "1250.00", high.
Routing: ap_pipeline goes to Data Engineering, ap_forecast to Data Science, ap_aging to Backend, ap_portal to Frontend; integration and end-to-end tests go to the Testing Agent.
Security and tenancy: no finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution; tier T2; the risk label is advisory only.
The feed schedule is unchanged: daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata. Feed v3 adds the optional paid_date column.
The design is consistent with D-2026-031 (calendar days), D-2026-044 (Decimal, never float) and D-2026-050 (paid invoices excluded), and applies L-007 (boundary at exactly 30) and L-011.
Current package versions: ap_pipeline 0.4.0, ap_forecast 0.9.0, ap_aging 1.4.0, ap_portal 2.3.0.

open_questions: TQ-1: bucket_for(30) returns '31-60', which does not match its own '1-30' label or the > 30 overdue rule. Fix it as a separate item (it changes aging totals), or accept it?
TQ-2: formatAmount uses Number(...).toFixed(2) against D-2026-044. Raise a separate item to fix the existing helper?
TQ-3: Approve the CT-1 overdue-list JSON contract and say who owns serialisation and transport between ap_aging and ap_portal (proposed: overdue_rows_to_json in ap_aging).
TQ-4: Confirm that risk is 'given' to build_explanation_request when it is not None.
TQ-5: Is counting early payments as 0 in the risk prediction (predict_delay_days behaviour) acceptable for this feature?
TQ-6: Confirm the row-class allow-list (an unexpected risk value renders risk-unknown).
TQ-7: Confirm the header-row form of renderOverdueRisk (plain <tr><th> with no thead) against the QA oracle.
TQ-8: Is sending the vendor's risk label to the external LLM provider (acme-llm) in the explanation prompt acceptable?
TQ-9: Should overdue_with_risk raise on an invoice without vendor, or treat it as 'unknown'?
TQ-10: For a row with invalid required fields and an invalid paid_date, keep today's reject reason or use 'paid_date' (a literal reading of AC-3)?
TQ-11: Accept string-only padding of amounts with fewer than two decimals in ap_portal, or display the CT-1 string strictly as received?

Carried unchanged: feat.prd OQ-B1 to OQ-B10 and PQ-1 to PQ-6 (the TRD proposes answers for OQ-B8, OQ-B10, PQ-1 and PQ-3 but leaves them open); feat.prototype PQ-P1 to PQ-P7; the earlier-step questions carried in feat.prd.
structured.summary: I rewrote feat.trd for FEAT-ZD-48600 in full. Every code citation now uses the GitHub repository names the read tracker records (ap-pipeline-sample, ap-forecast-sample, ap-aging-sample, ap-portal-sample), and I re-read each cited file in this attempt. This fixes all the G2 refusals. The TRD follows the TRD template. It states the current code baseline as cited findings F-1 to F-15, including two existing-code conflicts for the Architect: bucket_for(30) returns '31-60', and formatAmount formats through a binary float against D-2026-044. It then sets out components across the four coding lanes and the Testing lane, exact interfaces, a proposed JSON contract CT-1 between ap_aging and ap_portal, data, security and tenancy, 17 tests with explicit boundary cases, 11 risks, full PRD traceability and a decision-log check. There are 11 new non-blocking Architect questions (TQ-1 to TQ-11) and no blocking question.
